lines.text: Carrington. The beating heart of Manchester United.
A place built on hard work, on loyalty, and on a deep, unshakeable hatred of Leeds.
lines.delivery: same gravity all the way, then lean on 'hatred of Leeds'

lines.text: But one man believes the club has a mole.
Shhh. I am not here.
I am a defender. My job is to smell danger before it happens.
lines.delivery: talking head: calm, proud, very sincere

lines.text: And this building smells of Leeds.
lines.delivery: quiet, ominous, a little sniff before 'Leeds'

lines.text: Jason Wilcox. Director of football. Look at his career.
lines.delivery: like a detective presenting the suspect

lines.text: Blackburn. He won the league against United.
Leeds. I don't need to explain.
lines.delivery: flat, disgusted; the name says it all

lines.text: Manchester City.
Southampton. Okay, Southampton is fine.
This is not a CV. This is a criminal record.
Every day, he drinks his tea from a white mug. Why white, Jason? Why always white?
lines.delivery: building; 'Why white, Jason?' to the ceiling, unhinged

lines.text: When United score, he claps like this.
lines.delivery: flat; then he does one limp clap

lines.text: When Leeds score, I hear him in the toilet. Screaming.
In twenty nineteen, Leeds were caught spying on another club's training ground.
Lisandro considers this a tutorial.
Day one of the surveillance operation.
lines.delivery: serious, a little thrill in it

lines.text: Target is in the office. Target is drinking tea. White mug. Of course.
lines.delivery: whispered into a wrist like a secret agent

lines.text: Absolutely. We're fully aligned. Red through and through. One club, one vision, one process.
lines.delivery: smooth corporate phone voice, very pleased with himself

lines.text: At two fifty-eight, the director of football locked his door.
At two fifty-nine, he closed the blinds.
And at three o'clock... he let it breathe.
lines.delivery: long pause after 'three o'clock'; 'he let it breathe' almost tender

lines.text: Come on, Leeds. Come on, lads.
lines.delivery: an intimate whisper to the laptop

lines.text: Madre mía.
Yes! Get in! Marching on together!
lines.delivery: full-throated joy, singing the last two words

lines.text: I knew it!
lines.delivery: THE BIG ONE: a triumphant, furious shout

lines.text: The mole had been found. The plant did not survive.
lines.delivery: deadpan; a beat before 'The plant did not survive'

lines.text: Lisandro! This isn't what it looks like.
It looks like Leeds.
It's scouting. Data-led opposition scouting. I'm immersing myself in the enemy.
In their shirt?
Method scouting. It's very modern. You wouldn't understand, you were in a plant.
lines.delivery: trying to sound confident and failing

lines.text: Turn around.
You signed your own shirt?
It was a difficult time for me.
Oh, that's never a penalty, ref!
lines.delivery: he can't help it: a proper fan's shout at the laptop

lines.text: Say it.
Say what?
Leeds are rubbish.
Leeds are... r... really well coached, to be fair.
lines.delivery: straining to say it like it physically hurts, then it comes out warm and relieved

lines.text: He cannot say it. He is sick.
lines.delivery: to camera, heartbroken, like a doctor with bad news

lines.text: Mr Wilcox requested a right of reply.
Slide one. My commitment to Manchester United, as a percentage. Up eleven percent on last season.
Up from what?
We don't need to get into the baseline.
The presentation lasted seventy minutes.
Seventy minutes of PowerPoint. You know who else does this? Bielsa. Leeds. Case closed.
lines.delivery: talking head: building to a triumphant 'Case closed'

lines.text: I bleed red. I always have.
lines.delivery: talking head: sincere, hand on heart

lines.text: There might be a bit of white in there. That's medical.
lines.delivery: quieter, avoiding eye contact; rushed 'That's medical'

lines.text: So I go to the top. Omar will know what to do.
Omar! We have a mole!
I knew it.
Omar Berrada joined United from Manchester City. Lisandro had not done the reading.
lines.delivery: dry; a beat before 'Lisandro had not done the reading'

lines.text: That night, Lisandro Martinez believed he was the last loyal man at Carrington.
Vamos, Alexis. Vamos, hermano.
I knew it!
lines.delivery: the same triumphant shout Licho did

lines.text: It's Argentina! It's different!
He plays for Liverpool, Lisandro!
It's a red shirt.
Next time, on All or Something: Sir Jim, and his other football club.
Shhh. We are not here.
lines.delivery: hissed whisper (the same as his first line)

lines.text: We're not here.
lines.delivery: whispered back, very pleased to be included
